newsitem.title: UK: Chiroscience gives up most gains after meet.
newsitem.headline: Chiroscience gives up most gains after meet.

text.p: Shares in biotech group Chiroscience gave up most of their earlier gains to trade 1-1/2 pence higher at 414 on Monday after the company met analysts for a development update.

The share earlier hit a high of 442p but initial market enthusiasm over news that Chiroscience had selected two anti-cancer drugs for human trials was tempered by disappointment the tests were not starting now, but only at the end of the year, analysts said.
There are also technical problems around the development of certain tests to run in conjunction with clinical trials for Chiroscience's drug against arthritis, they added.
It was unclear whether the anti-arthritis compound was going to enter phase II trials, analysts said.
These negative impacts were, however, offset by the good progress made in getting local anaesthetic Levobupivacaine to market.
"The local anaesthetic product is doing extremely well. If they get the pricing right they should get a very large slice of that market segment," said analyst John Savin at Greig Middleton.

He was also pleased by asthma drug D4418 going into clinical trials in May. "That programme is looking good, but overall it (Chiroscience) is fairly valued. There is not much to drive the price," Savin said.
